positions.assessment: The Normal Summon is used and Vata's once-per-turn hand summon is spent, so the only real choices are Ahrima's discard-for-Lair or keeping Ahrima. Both lines end with Enemy Controller Set, so the card count is the same either way. Kept in hand, Ahrima can be Normal Summoned next turn and Tribute a DARK monster to search Simoon. That is the deck's core engine card and worth more than Lair right now. Lair is a fine card, but with Ahrima discarded it loses its best partner.

grades.label: A
grades.reason: This Sets Enemy Controller for the opponent's turn and keeps Ahrima for a Simoon search next turn, which is the higher-value use of the card.

grades.label: B
grades.reason: Searching Lair costs no cards, but it trades Ahrima's Simoon-search potential for a field spell whose best synergy (Ahrima) is gone. It is playable but clearly the weaker use of the card.

positions.assessment: Boreastorm needs to become Lv2 for Full Armor Master with BWD (8), so Chinook, Vata or Harmattan all work. The question is which one to lose from the Deck. Once BWD is banished for Assault Dragon, Vata's main effect is dead, and two more Vatas remain in the Deck. Harmattan is a singleton level-fixer, and Chinook is a strong quick negate/-700 card that is better left as a live draw.

grades.label: A
grades.reason: It makes the combo work, but it sends away Chinook, one of the deck's best interactive cards on later turns, when Vata was nearly dead.

grades.label: B
grades.reason: Vata is the least useful Lv2 in the Deck once BWD is banished, and the reasoning is correct.

grades.label: C
grades.reason: It reaches the right Level and keeps Chinook in the Deck, but it thins the singleton Harmattan instead of a nearly dead Vata.

positions.assessment: The opponent's field is empty, so Dark Armed Dragon could only destroy my own cards. Nobody can attack on turn 1. Setting Delta Crow lets it destroy face-down Spells/Traps the opponent Sets on their turn, which is a free gain before ending.

grades.label: A
grades.reason: Setting Delta Crow is the only useful action left. It readies backrow removal for the opponent's turn, and DAD has no target.
